free_tier.stated: 100 projects; 100 CU-hours per project; 1 GB Postgres storage per project and 20 GB per account; 10 branches per project; 5 GB public network transfer per project per month; 5 GB object storage
free_tier.notes: Free autoscales to 2 CU (8 GB RAM); scale-to-zero after 5 min is always on and cannot be disabled

per_object_cap.stated: 1 GB of Postgres storage per project; exceeding it blocks writes rather than billing
per_object_cap.notes: 999 GiB is the branch logical size limit on the claimed project, not the free allowance

retention.stated: no deletion on free. Exceeding CU-hours or the 5 GB transfer suspends compute until the next billing period; exceeding storage blocks writes. 'None of these limits delete your data'
retention.notes: an unclaimed Claimable Neon project expires in 72 hours instead

egress.terms: 5 GB public network transfer per project per month included; exceeding it suspends compute until the next billing period
egress.price_per_tb: USD 0.10/GB on Launch and Scale after 500 GB

interface_detail: Postgres wire protocol over TLS on a -pooler or direct host; a Management API and the Neon CLI; a Data API for HTTP queries
tooling: any Postgres client (psql, psycopg, pg8000, Prisma, Drizzle); rclone does not apply
chaining: a free Postgres behind a free Worker or a tunnel gives a public endpoint with no card

limits.value: 100 CU-hours per project per month; a 0.25 CU minimum means about 400 wall-clock hours of a minimum-size database, and autoscaling to 2 CU quarters that
compute suspends after 5 minutes idle on Free and the setting cannot be disabled
1 GB storage per project, 20 GB per account; writes are blocked at the cap
5 GB public network transfer per project per month; exceeding it suspends compute

limits_note: connection pooling accepts up to 10,000 client connections in transaction mode; max_connections was 450 on the observed compute and is capped at 4,000 above 9 CU

identity_cost.detail: email signup for a normal account; the Claimable path provisions a project with no signup, no card and no email, and the project expires in 72 hours unless claimed

reliability_note: the unclaimed path is a 72-hour demo: 100 MB storage, 1 GB transfer, then the project expires; commit latency on a cold anonymous project measured 1,750 ms
confidence_note: the 100 MB cap was reached and its SQLSTATE recorded. The free-plan figures are a first-party page.

evidence.proved: POST with type anonymous returned 201 in 4.5 s, provisioning project lucky-queen-53359445 in aws-us-east-2 with expires_at 2026-10-25T02:41:43Z; 1480 bytes; no signup, no card, no email
grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer with the identity assertion returned 200 and a 3600-second bearer token; the token-exchange grant type is rejected with a 400
200 with a working postgresql:// URI only when database_name and role_name are supplied; without them the proxy returns 502 with an upstream decode error

PostgreSQL 17.11 connected in 2619 ms over TLS; create table, insert and select returned hello-f-research; max_connections 450; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 5min; vector 0.8.0, postgis 3.5.7, timescaledb 2.17.1 and pg_trgm available

SHOW returns 100MB; filling with 500 kB rows failed at SQLSTATE 53100 with 'could not extend file because project size limit (100 MB) has been exceeded', hint naming neon.max_cluster_size and pagestore_smgr.c:throttle_or_fail_extension, after 70 rows and 78 MB of reported database size
ten single-row autocommit inserts averaged 1,750.6 ms each on a cold anonymous project; 35 MB of bulk insert took 21.8 s, or 1.61 MB/s
100 projects, 100 CU-hours/project, 1 GB/project and 20 GB/account storage, 5 GB egress/project, scale-to-zero after 5 min on Free, and the sentence that none of the limits delete data
5 GB per project per month included on Free; exceeding it suspends compute until the next billing cycle
PgBouncer transaction mode accepts up to 10,000 client connections, pools sized at 0.9 x max_connections
unclaimed projects expire in 72 hours and are capped at 100 MB storage and 1 GB transfer; claim codes expire in 15 minutes

evidence.url: probe:create extension vector on the claimable project
evidence.proved: CREATE EXTENSION vector succeeded in 1.1 s and pg_extension reported version 0.8.0; a vector(3) column, an insert of two rows and an ORDER BY e <-> '[1,2,3]' KNN query returned distances 0.0 and 5.196 in order; run after dropping the fill, bulk and lat tables from the cap probe, at which point the database was 7440 kB
PgBouncer transaction mode accepts up to 10,000 client connections; pool size defaults to 90% of max_connections

notes: Storage is generous and compute is not. 100 projects x 1 GB is 100 GB nominal, but each project also gets 100 CU-hours, so the shape is 100 small workloads and not one 100 GB database. The free tier does not delete data; it suspends compute or blocks writes. The measured 100 MB cap belongs to the anonymous Claimable path, not the free plan, and conflating them is the easy error. The vector extension was installed and queried, not merely listed as available, so `pgvector on a free Postgres` is a working chain and not an inference.
